VINE CURTAIN OVER THE DOORWAY: a heavy curtain of glossy vine hanging across a stone doorway, leaves layered in three greens, a few long tendrils swinging free of the stone face and catching the air
CORDS LACING THE ARCH: thick creeper cords woven back and forth across a stone arch, each cord wrapped in small paired leaves, the whole web of green pulling the stones into a soft embrace

WALL STITCHED IN SMALL LEAVES: one broad wall covered edge to edge in a creeper of tiny rounded leaves, each leaf a single bright pixel of green, the mortar lines still readable beneath the living skin

FLOWERING CREEPER AT THE WINDOW: a creeper spilling over the sill of a stone window opening, its stems tumbling down the outer face in loose ropes, small yellow blossoms dotting the length of every cord
TENDRILS REACHING ACROSS THE GAP: slim green tendrils stretched across an open gap between two stone piers, each tendril hooked at its tip, the whole fine mesh trembling slightly in the still air
ROOTS POURED DOWN THE WALL: a broad tree riding the wall top, its pale roots poured down the face in thick cords that grip each block and knit together as they reach the ground
ROOTS GRIPPING THE BLOCK: a single large root arm curved over a fallen block, its four thick fingers pressed into the stone face, the pale wood worn smooth where it meets the carved edge
ROOTS LIFTING THE FLAGSTONES: tree roots running below a paved floor, each root swelling just enough to lift its flagstone into a gentle wave, the joints between stones opened into long bright cracks
ROOT ARCH THROUGH THE GAP: a root that entered a gap between two lintels and grew until it arched back out the other side, its loop now a second doorway of pale living wood set inside the stone one
MOSS ON EVERY STAIR TREAD: a deep fur of soft moss covering every horizontal tread of a stone stair, the green thick enough to show footfall shapes, the vertical risers still bare pale stone
LICHEN ON THE PILLAR: pale grey-green lichen spread across a round pillar in irregular patches, each patch a soft island with a clean edge, the whole surface dappled in quiet green and stone
FERNS FROM THE CRACKS: ferns unrolling from every horizontal crack in a block wall, each frond pale and tightly coiled at its tip, the older fronds spread flat against the stone face in dark fans

VELVET CAP ON THE DRUM: a fallen column drum lying on its side with a thick cap of velvet moss grown across its entire upper face, the green surface smooth and slightly domed, the stone edge still crisp below
SLIM TREE THROUGH THE STAIRWELL: a slim tree growing straight up through the open centre of a spiral stairwell, its trunk rising past each landing in turn, its canopy now level with the topmost step
CANOPY ON THE ROOFLESS CHAMBER: a broad tree grown inside a roofless stone chamber, its canopy spreading flat across the wall tops as a living green roof, the chamber below held in soft shade

SAPLINGS ALONG THE WALL TOP: young saplings rooted in the soil along a wall's top course, their slim trunks leaning at uneven intervals, their roots already feeling their way down between the upper blocks
GREEN WATER ACROSS THE FLOOR: clear green water standing still across a stone floor, the submerged blocks visible through it in soft wavering lines, a faint green light rising from the water surface

SEAGRASS ON THE SUBMERGED BLOCKS: ribbons of seagrass rooted between submerged stone blocks, each ribbon leaning together with its neighbours in the slow current, small bright corals crusting the lower faces of the stones

SPRING THROUGH THE FLAGSTONES: a spring welling up through a gap between two flagstones, the water rising in a slow clear dome before spreading in a thin sheet across the surrounding floor, the stone around the gap furred in bright green algae

WATER FROM THE BROKEN CHANNEL: a thin sheet of water dropping from the broken lip of a stone channel, falling in a clean arc into a pool on the floor below, the stone face beneath the break stained in a long stripe of dark green

DUNES TO THE PILLAR'S WAIST: smooth sand dunes banked against leaning stone pillars of uneven height, each dune curving up to a pillar's waist in a clean arc, one windward face scoured pale and its leeward side half-buried

SAND FAN THROUGH THE DOORWAY: sand drifted through a stone doorway in a broad fan across the floor inside, the fan's leading edge a clean curved line, the deepest part of the drift pressed tight against the door jambs
FLOOR HALF-BURIED IN SAND: a paved floor buried under drifted sand, only the top edges of the largest blocks still showing above the surface, the sand between them smooth and unmarked

WILDFLOWERS ON THE FALLEN TERRACE: wildflowers grown thick across a fallen terrace, their stems pushing up between every crack in the tumbled stones, the whole surface a close mat of small white and yellow blooms

BLOSSOM TREE OVER THE COURTYARD WALL: one old blossom tree leaning in over a low courtyard wall from one side, its branches reaching well across the top course of stone, clusters of pale pink blossom hanging above the wall face and dropping petals onto the stones below
